translation_notes: Each SELECT ... OPTIONAL ... FILTER(!bound(...)) query becomes s{ }: m{ } has no OPTIONAL/FILTER, so this is the only fit.

RML_* names are plain Python strings holding IRIs (not URIRef), so bare {RML_X} interpolation in term position coerces to a Literal and silently matches nothing; each use is wrapped {rdflib.term.URIRef(RML_X)} to keep the predicate an IRI, exactly the coercion trap in INSTRUCTIONS.md 2 bis.

@graph mapping_graph must NOT be followed by a trailing '.' inside a function body: with the dot, the transpiler mis-balances the braces of every s{ } that follows and raises a plain SyntaxError -- confirmed by a minimal repro; worth reporting upstream as a lexer/oracle gap.
Context shim rml_constants.py reconstructs the RML_* IRI constants from morph_kgc/constants.py at the pinned commit (not in the extracted context lines).
The .add() calls stay one per loop body (six independent loops): no join is introduced, so cardinality matches the original exactly.

repair.remaining: Jugement non traité (drapeau wrong-construction) : les six +{ } gardent {rdflib.term.URIRef(RML_…)} au lieu de f<{RML_…}> (équivalent selon le triage ; dans les s{ } la forme f<{…}> est refusée par le parseur SPARQL).

optimization_notes: optimized.py: five of the six rules have the same body (`for term_map, _ in query: add((term_map, TERM_TYPE, X))`). A local helper `complete(termtype, query)` replaces them and takes the query inline, so the `query = ... \` variables go. `rdflib.term.URIRef(RML_TERM_TYPE)` is computed once as term_type. The queries keep their f-string text with the RML_* constants, because the repository keeps its IRIs in constants. They stay sequential, because each rule sees the termtypes that the rules before it added.
optimized.py, what was not done: a rewrite in triple-pattern calls (OPTIONAL/FILTER !bound as `not in` tests) is longer. A single VALUES query for the four rules of the last loop is also longer.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: the same helper, whose body is `+{ {term_map} {term_type} f<{termtype}> }`. The queries are `s{ }` with `f<{RML_X}>` and `{term_type}` as initial bindings, which is shorter than the `{rdflib.term.URIRef(RML_X)}` of translated.ldpy.

Rule 5 (referencing object maps) is a pure BGP, so it becomes `list(m{ ?term_map f<{RML_PARENT_TRIPLES_MAP}> [ f<{RML_SUBJECT_MAP}> [ {term_type} ?termtype ] ] })`: the nested blank nodes are the non-projected intermediate variables. The `list()` is needed for exactness: m{ } is a lazy join over triples(), and a termtype added during the iteration could otherwise feed a later solution. The SPARQL result is materialised before the adds. This is the notation (the most specific island for a BGP), not a restructuring.

The notation ratio is above 1 (1.22) because the tokenizer counts a Python query string as one token per string piece, but counts the SPARQL inside `s{ }` token by token. The `s{ }` text is not longer than the f-string text. No exception to the symmetry rule.
header_optimization_notes: Nothing unused in the header: rdflib and the sixteen RML_* constants are all used on both sides, so optimized_header.py and optimized_header.ldpy are byte copies of the optimized artefacts.
